## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4d57a2336462903dca941af12612214469728abf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/agents/os-dev.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/reading-discipline.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-post-protocol.md + scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

PR #32962 for card #32873, net diff against `main` at the head: 7 files, +20 −12. `main` has moved two commits past the merge base; neither touches `.claude/**` or `scripts/pm/**`.

- **Accept-set and public surface: none.** Six `.claude/**` rule files and one root `scripts/pm` tool; no package path, no schema, no export. In `check-half-states.mjs` the diff changes one line comment, one JSDoc block and the string literals of two finding sentences. No predicate, no constant (`QUEUE_ON_DUTY_UNCLAIMED_HOURS` stays 2 at :15540) and no pin moves. Right.
- **Rule-surface changes, each named.**
  - `reading-discipline.md:35`: clause order only; no duty added or removed. Right.
  - `os-dev.md:56`: a pointer into `SKILL.md` becomes the definition in place, in the words of `SKILL.md:285`. Right.
  - `platform-readings.md`: one reading out (main :410), one reading in (head :424). The one removed survives outside the file. Right; see ③.
  - `SKILL.md:201`: changes who reads a skills-lane pure-code PR, from the seat itself to an at-tier re-review through a sub-agent or card thread. It agrees with `execution-duties.md:122` on the route and collides with `contract-review.md:20` on whether a second agent starts at all. Wrong as a pair: finding A.
  - `contract-review.md:20–21`: the at-tier review is no longer "in the seat"; the tier is taken through a sub-agent or card thread, and the quota clause at :21 follows from it. Right against `execution-duties.md:122–123`.
  - `seat-post-protocol.md:18`: a cron change joins the stub-refresh triggers, which :65 already implies by recording the CRON on the stub. Right.
- **Line ratchet** (ceiling rows in `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` on the head; the diff does not touch that file): `os-dev.md` 405 of 405 (:1809), `SKILL.md` 319 of 319 (:413), `contract-review.md` 60 of 60 (:578), `platform-readings.md` 458 of 458 (:1160), `reading-discipline.md` 37 of 37 (:1367), `seat-post-protocol.md` 88 of 88 (:1268). Every count equals the count on `main`. No line is added, so `SKILL.md` owes no ruling id. No re-wrap: each hunk replaces whole lines one for one, and `platform-readings.md` is one line out, one line in.
- **120-byte cap:** the seven new lines measure 116, 117, 119, 99, 120, 117 and 120 bytes. None is over.
- **id-lint:** zero matches of the issue-number pattern in any of the six files on the head, the new lines included.
- **Pins:** no gate, self-test or workflow on the head quotes any of the seven replaced sentences (each searched in `scripts/` and `.github/`). The H70 and H71 text pins (:28680, :28699) name strings the new sentences still carry; the 1h59m and 2h01m window pin (:28690) is untouched. The handoff template line that `record-recognisers.mjs` pins verbatim (`contract-review.md:22`) is untouched.
- **Check-runs on the head**, read 2026-11-13T01:20Z: 54 runs, 30 success, 23 skipped, 1 cancelled.
  - `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is success. That job holds the steps `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet`, `pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint` and `pnpm check:pm-half-states` (`lint.yml` :1062, :1072, :1281), so the ratchet, the id-lint and the sweeper's own battery are green on this head.
  - `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core` are success.
  - `Live half-state sweep` is **cancelled**. Its annotation reads "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 15m0s". The step "Sweep the board and update the anchor" started 2026-11-13T00:59Z and was cancelled 2026-11-13T01:14Z with no output; the later steps were skipped. That is NOT MEASURED: neither red nor green. The diff changes no executed logic in the script, and the ten pull-request runs of this workflow before this one each finished in under 12 minutes, so the 15-minute cap is the likely cause. That is a likelihood, not a reading. No base run exists to compare a signature against, because the workflow runs only on pull requests that touch the patrol.
  - This is not a finding on the diff. It is a landing prerequisite: Tier S lifts on a PASS record and on every check being green (`AGENTS.md:290`), so the seat re-runs that job before it queues the PR. A re-run does not move the head, and this record still covers it. If the job times out again, the sweep's runtime against its cap is a card of its own.
  - I did not judge the 23 skips against the expected-skip roster. That reading belongs to the landing pre-check.

### ② Semver level

- No changeset is in the diff and none is owed. `.claude/**` and root `scripts/pm/**` ship in no package; the root manifest is private. The PR carries `skip-changeset`, and `Check Changeset` is success on the head.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand at line start in the PR body and match the claim. Right: nothing published widens, narrows or changes meaning.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag 1, the paying cut in `platform-readings.md`** (the dev: "Judgment call, flagged for the contract review"). Holds. The file's header ranks tools before text, and the removed reading is held by tools: `check-half-states.mjs` :21143–21149, `board-snapshot.mjs` :2138, `check-expected-skips.mjs` :1061 and `close-cards.mjs` :625 each print "capture it BEFORE any pipe" in their own output. `os-dev.md:168–173` teaches the trap in full. In the same table :395 already tells a seat to take the printed verdict line and never the code. The card's Acceptance line asks for a same-file payment where a file is at its ceiling, and the standing increment exception in `triage-duties.md:98` permits a raise but does not order one. Nit E records what the cut costs.
- **Flag 2, H71's clock stays at 2 with a rewritten reason.** Holds; argued in ④ under the implementing file. Nits C and D are on its wording.
- **`os-dev.md:356` left as is.** Holds. The line says the dispatch order pastes the frame verbatim and the dev keeps no copy, and :357 tells the dev to ask the PM when the order did not carry it. Neither sentence sends a thread to open `SKILL.md`.
- **Reference header lines left as is** (the card: "judge and say which way"). Holds. The exact phrase is on `dispatch-runbook.md:3` alone, as the PR says. Six more headers point into `SKILL.md` by section name (`coordinator.md:4`, `decision-analysis.md:3`, `state-machine.md:3`, `true-green.md:3`, `lanes/director.md:3`, `lanes/ui.md:3`). The same judgment covers them: each scopes its file for a seat reader, and a thread's own rule is `dispatch-runbook.md:143`.
- **The separator in `seat-post-protocol.md:18`** became a space to fit 120 bytes. Holds: typographic, and :65 and `seat-lifecycle.md:38` still spell the two keys apart.
- **Raised here, not flagged by the dev:** the choice behind finding A. Rewriting `SKILL.md:201` as a routed at-tier review keeps a per-lane review duty on a diff that touches no review face. If the lane means to keep that duty, it is a rule about who reviews what, and it wants the maintainer's word (`lanes/skills.md:18`). If not, the line can say what the by-face rule already decides, and no ruling is needed.
- **The new reading at `platform-readings.md:424`** is the card thread's own measurement. A read-only review cannot re-measure a thread's roster. Its consequence is the order `dispatch-runbook.md:143` already gives, so a wrong first half would cost one redundant read and nothing else.
- **open_questions:** none in the inputs. The card carries no dev report; the PR body's two open items are flags 1 and 2.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. There is no out-of-relay author to name.
- **Surface:** every hunk lies inside the claim's declared file surface. `seat-lifecycle.md` and `AGENTS.md` are untouched.

### ④ Design judgment

**`reading-discipline.md:35` — holds.** The line equals the card's Part 1 spelling, 117 bytes before and after. The carve-out now closes the line, after the outsourcing clause, so 「仍」 reads as the exception to it. It agrees with `dispatch-runbook.md:58–60` (state reads outsource, ruling-grade reads do not) and with `execution-duties.md:11` (the seat reads each candidate in full). Tried: does the outsourcing clause, now next to the CI-log clause, read as "outsource long CI logs"? It names 「长线程」, so no.

**`os-dev.md:56` — holds.** The parenthesis is the definition at `SKILL.md:285`, word for word. The half of :285 that is a seat's rule (「无则第二次即开」) is rightly not copied, because a dev files no card (`os-dev.md:57`, `SKILL.md:283`). Tried the other target the card names: `triage-duties.md:74` uses the term and does not define it, so a retarget there would not have closed the gap. In place is the right choice. Its cost is that the definition now lives in two files with no sync gate; the card's own wording accepts that.

**`platform-readings.md` — holds.** The row at :424 is 120 bytes, one fact on one line, no id, under 〈读数陷阱〉 beside the harness rows. It agrees with `dispatch-runbook.md:143`, and it gives that clause's reason a home, which is the card's Part 3. It is more exact than the clause the earlier PR dropped: the type is listed, the body is not loaded. The paying cut is answered in ③ flag 1.

**`SKILL.md:201` and `contract-review.md:20` — finding A, should-fix.** For a skills-lane PR that touches only `scripts/pm/`, the two lines now give opposite orders. Such a diff touches none of the four faces: `reviewFace` returns no hit for a `scripts/pm` path, and this PR's own hits are the six `.claude` files. `contract-review.md:20` says 「四面皆不碰 ⇒ CI 加席位自读 ⛔ 不起第二个 agent」, and :7 says 「欠不欠按面判 ⛔ 不按车道」. `SKILL.md:201` now says the same diff lands 「经子代理或卡线程达档复审(清单不减)后」. Before this PR both lines said the seat reads it itself (「由本席按达档自审」, 「达档者席内审」), and the at-tier part cost nothing, because line 122 then put only the seats outside the skills lane at the default tier. With every seat at the default tier, the rewritten :201 turns that incidental tier into a duty, by lane, to start a contract-tier agent for a diff that owes no contract review. That is the spend the seat-tier rule was written to cut, and :7 rules out a duty by lane.

The bullet at :20 also reads badly on its own now. It forbids a second agent and then, after a semicolon and with no change of subject, routes the tier through a sub-agent. The nearest reading applies both halves to the no-face case. That is the clause-junction defect this card's Part 1 repairs in `reading-discipline.md:35`. The second half also says 「档」 without qualification, while the declaration face's `TIER_DEFAULT` record stays in the seat (:13, `execution-duties.md:123`).

Two ways out, both in place and inside the byte cap. (a) :201 says the seat reads its own pure-code PR itself, at its own tier, which is what :7, :20 and `execution-duties.md:122–123` already decide; no new duty. (b) The lane keeps an at-tier pass on its own tooling; then :20 must name the exception, and ③ says whose word that needs. Either way the second half of :20 should mark its subject. One spelling that fits at 120 bytes: 「…⛔ 不起第二个 agent;欠审 ⇒ 派发席经子代理或卡线程取档。」

It is not a must-fix. A no-face diff owes no contract review under either line, so neither reading lands a governed change unreviewed. The cost of the split is a wasted contract-tier agent, or a seat unsure which line governs.

**`contract-review.md:21` — holds.** 「取档」 picks up the route :20 names, and the handoff template on :22 is unchanged. The retired fuse phrases that the dispatch-gates self-test refuses are not reintroduced.

**`seat-post-protocol.md:18` — holds.** :65 records `Patrol: TRIGGER_ID · CRON` on the stub and asks a relaxation to note its reason. A stub refreshed only on seating, queue change, wall and handover would go stale at the first switch to standby. Tried: does any reader parse this line? None does; H70 reads the seat post, not this file.

**`scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` (implementing) — agrees with the contract**, sentence by sentence against `execution-duties.md:166–167` and `seat-post-protocol.md:65`.

- :15502, the section comment: "patrol routine". Agrees.
- :15535–15538, the clock's JSDoc: "every 45 minutes or less" is :166. "Two missed patrols plus slack" is 45 + 45 + 30 minutes, which is the constant. The standby sentence is :166. The last clause is nit C.
- :15571–15574, H70: the cadence parenthesis is :166. One routine with two cadences agrees with `seat-lifecycle.md:38` and with the cron-change trigger this PR adds at `seat-post-protocol.md:18`.
- :15612–15617, H71: the in-flight sentence agrees. The standby sentence agrees with :166–167: the mailbox table in `project-forms.md` has no key for a newly queued card, so a card that reaches a standby lane does wait for the fallback patrol, and "under ~6 h" is that patrol's upper bound.
- No "hourly" remains for a project seat's patrol. The other uses in the file are the triage Routine's tier and one fixture of a live post.
- Tried to break the clock. At 2 h the row fires on a standby lane for a state the rule now allows up to about 6 h. The row is report-only, an H row is a reading and never a precondition (`execution-duties.md:3`), and the sentence names the standby case. So an early fire costs a reader one sentence, where a 6 h clock would hide a stalled in-flight lane for four more hours and move a pin. Keeping 2 holds.

**Nits.** None affects correctness or the contract.

- B, nit: `SKILL.md:201` and `contract-review.md:20` say 「子代理」 where `execution-duties.md:122–123` say 「隔离子代理」. The isolation rule survives at `contract-review.md:44–45`, and the lines have no byte room (117 and 119 of 120). Accepted deviation.
- C, nit: `check-half-states.mjs:15537–15538` says "no seat post states standby machine-readably". The stub's `Patrol:` line carries a CRON by rule, and :18 as edited here keeps it current. What is true today is narrower: the value is free text and unjudged (the module's own fixture at :28664 is a live prose spelling). A later card could read a parseable cron with the module's existing `cronPeriodHours` and give a standby lane its own clock. That is a behaviour change and is rightly not in this diff.
- D, nit: `check-half-states.mjs:15615–15616` says a card "may only be waiting for that patrol" and does not say where the reader learns that the lane is on standby, which is the lane seat post's `Patrol:` line.
- E, nit: after the cut in `platform-readings.md`, the pipe-status trap has one prose home, `os-dev.md:168–173`, which is the dev's file. `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs:903` still tells the removed row as part of the eleventh increment; that is history and stays true as history. No edit owed.
- F, nit, follow-up card: `SKILL.md:190` 「席只达档补审现 head 记录未盖处」 is the same class as N6, eleven lines above the edited line. The card did not name it, so its absence is not a defect of this PR. `AGENTS.md:290` 「席内达档复核落地」 reads the same way; it is outside the claim's surface and was read, not reviewed.

**Findings:** A should-fix (`SKILL.md:201` with `contract-review.md:20`). B, C, D, E, F nits. No must-fix. A's fix moves the head and earns a delta review; the seat may instead carry A to a follow-up card and land this head.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `479054bc885797f4af1df05b32f27706ddf124c1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/agents/os-dev.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/reading-discipline.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-post-protocol.md + scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs

### ① Derived judgments

This is the delta review of finding A in the record at PR comment 6841013971, which reviewed head 4d57a233 of PR #32962 (card #32873). It judges the fix and what moved with it. Everything that did not move keeps that record's judgment.

- **What moved: one line.** The new head is one commit on top of the reviewed head. The diff between the two heads is `SKILL.md:201` alone, one line for one line. The other five `hits` files and `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` are byte-identical to the reviewed head. The net diff against `main` is still 7 files, +20 −12, and `main` has not moved.
- **The rule-surface change.** `SKILL.md:201` now reads 「skills 车道自有 PR:纯代码面如 `scripts/pm/` 由本席自读(清单不减)后落地。」 The seat reads its own pure-code PR itself; the line no longer names a tier or a second agent. Right: it now says what `contract-review.md:7` and `:20` and `execution-duties.md:122–123` already decide. Argued in ④.
- **Accept-set and public surface:** none, as before. No package path, no schema, no export.
- **Line ratchet:** `SKILL.md` 319 of 319 (ceiling row :413 in `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, a file the PR does not touch). The other five files are unchanged at their ceilings: `os-dev.md` 405, `contract-review.md` 60, `platform-readings.md` 458, `reading-discipline.md` 37, `seat-post-protocol.md` 88. No line is added, so no ruling id is owed. No re-wrap.
- **120-byte cap:** the new line is 96 bytes.
- **id-lint:** zero matches of the issue-number pattern in any of the six files on the new head.
- **Pins:** no script, self-test or workflow on the new head quotes the old sentence or the new one.
- **Check-runs on the new head**, read 2026-11-13T01:42Z: 53 runs, 30 success, 22 skipped, 1 cancelled, none in progress.
  - `Lint · repo & tooling gates` is success. It holds the ratchet, the id-lint and the sweeper's own battery.
  - `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core` are success.
  - `Check Changeset` is skipped in both suites on this head. The job-level condition in `pr-automation.yml` (:308–309) skips a PR whose event already carries `skip-changeset`. On the earlier head one run was success because the label landed after the event and was read live. Both shapes say the same thing: no changeset is owed.
  - `Live half-state sweep` is **cancelled again**, with the same signature as on the earlier head. The annotation reads "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 15m0s". The step "Sweep the board and update the anchor" started 2026-11-13T01:27Z and was cancelled 2026-11-13T01:42Z; the later steps were skipped. That is NOT MEASURED a second time, on two heads that carry the same bytes of the script.
  - It is still not a finding on the diff: the PR changes string literals and comments in that script, and this delta commit does not touch it at all. But two timeouts in a row say a plain re-run is unlikely to clear it. The sweep's runtime against its 15-minute cap is now a defect of the patrol, for a card of its own. No base run exists to compare against, because the workflow runs only on pull requests that touch the patrol.
  - The landing consequence stands and is the seat's to dispose of before queueing: Tier S lifts on a PASS record and on every check being green (`AGENTS.md:290`), and `SKILL.md:204–206` gives the seat's rule for a red that is not required. A cancelled run is not green and is not one of the three "red by design" conditions. This record does not clear it. The PR's `mergeable_state` reads `unstable`.
  - As before, I did not judge the 22 skips against the expected-skip roster.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged. No changeset is in the diff and none is owed: `.claude/**` and root `scripts/pm/**` ship in no package. The PR still carries `skip-changeset`.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` still stand at line start in the PR body. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The flag the first record raised** (the choice behind finding A) is answered by the fix. The lane took the way that keeps no per-lane review duty, so no maintainer's word is needed.
- **What the fix gives up, said plainly.** Before the seat-tier rule landed, the skills seat read this class of PR at the contract tier, because that was the seat's own tier. Now it reads it at the default tier. That drop is the effect of `execution-duties.md:122`, which was on `main` before this PR. It is not a gate weakened here: a diff that touches no review face never owed a contract review (`contract-review.md:7`), and 「清单不减」 keeps the seat's checklist whole.
- **PR body.** As read 2026-11-13T01:33Z, the N6 bullet already quotes the new `:201` wording and names finding A. The Verification section still calls 4d57a233 "the final head". That is prose, outside this record; the seat refreshes it.
- **Dev flags 1 and 2 and the other flags of the first record** stand unchanged. The files they concern did not move.
- **open_questions:** none in the inputs.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`. There is no out-of-relay author to name.
- **Surface:** the delta commit lies inside the claim's declared file surface (`SKILL.md:201`).

### ④ Design judgment

**`SKILL.md:201` — finding A is closed.** A's ground was that two lines gave opposite orders for a skills-lane PR that touches only `scripts/pm/`. They now agree.

- Against `contract-review.md:7` (「欠不欠按面判 ⛔ 不按车道」): the line no longer creates a review duty by lane. A `scripts/pm` path hits neither the schema face nor the rules face in `reviewFace`, so with `Clause-②: no` nothing is owed, and :201 asks for nothing beyond the seat's own read.
- Against `contract-review.md:20` (「四面皆不碰 ⇒ CI 加席位自读 ⛔ 不起第二个 agent」): :201 uses the same word, 「自读」, and names no second agent.
- Against `execution-duties.md:122–123`: the line no longer asks the seat for a tier it never holds, and it does not route a tier where none is owed. :123's 「余面未达档 ⛔ 不自审」 is about the review faces; a no-face diff is not one of them.
- Tried to break it. Does 「自读」 read as "no review"? No: 「(清单不减)」 keeps the checklist, and the PR still passes CI and the seat's ACCEPT. Does it reach a mixed diff? No: 「纯代码面」 limits it, and a diff that also touches a face goes by face (`contract-review.md:14`), as this PR itself does. Does it collide with :202 or :207? No: :202 is the governed faces, and :207 keeps the PM's own tool PRs with the maintainer.

**`contract-review.md:20` — unchanged; the rest of A, graded on its own as nit G.** The first record also said the second half of :20 should mark its subject, and that 「档」 there is unqualified. That part was not edited. Standing alone it is a nit, and I regrade it openly as one, for three reasons. The junction 「;谁跑 = 派发席,…」 is on `main` already; this PR changed only what follows it. Read as one topic, the bullet now contradicts its own ⛔ and contradicts :201, which pushes a reader to the split reading. And no line anywhere now tells a seat to start an agent for a no-face diff, so the misreading has nothing to lean on. It has no effect on correctness or the contract. Disposition: accepted deviation, or the follow-up card that carries nit F; a fix here would move the head.

**The other five files and `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`** are byte-identical to the reviewed head. Their judgments in the first record stand: each holds.

**Nits carried from the first record.** None affects correctness or the contract.

- B, nit: now on `contract-review.md:20` alone, since :201 no longer says 「子代理」. Accepted deviation.
- C, nit: `check-half-states.mjs:15537–15538`, "no seat post states standby machine-readably" overstates.
- D, nit: `check-half-states.mjs:15615–15616`, the standby sentence does not say where the reader learns the lane is on standby.
- E, nit: the pipe-status trap's one prose home is `os-dev.md:168–173`; no edit owed.
- F, nit, follow-up card: `SKILL.md:190` 「席只达档补审」 is the same class as N6.
- G, nit, new in this record: the unmarked subject and unqualified 「档」 in `contract-review.md:20`, above.

**Findings:** A closed. No must-fix and no should-fix remains. B, C, D, E, F, G are nits, so the review round ends here. The one open item is not a finding: `Live half-state sweep` has no verdict on this head.

domain:skills#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cwhy7iXYvfs2NorugV

Landing under a maintainer exception, at 2026-11-13T02:25Z, head `479054bc885797f4af1df05b32f27706ddf124c1`.

- Contract review: PASS 6841013971 on `4d57a233`, delta PASS 6841341189 on this head (finding A closed; nits only).
- Check-runs on this head: 30 success, 22 skipped, 1 cancelled, 0 failed. The cancelled one is `Live half-state sweep` (half-state-patrol.yml, report-only, not one of the eleven required checks), which hit its 15-minute cap on both heads with no output: NOT MEASURED, cause unproven. This PR changes only strings and comments in that script, and the script's self-test battery is green in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`.
